stopShip.title: Per-app credit wallets and aggregate financial activity are publicly readable despite a configured API key
evidence: packages/core/core/relay-node/api.js:979-1035 dispatches all four credit GET routes before any _requireAuth call
packages/core/core/relay-node/api-credits.js:82-101 returns appPubkey, balance, totalDeposited, totalSpent, bonus totals, and activity timestamps

A loopback HTTP probe started RelayAPI with apiKey=configured-secret and no Authorization header; /api/v1/credits/stats and /api/v1/credits/wallets both returned HTTP 200 with the seeded wallet and its financial totals
dashboard/payments.html:565-587 sends an empty x-api-key header, not the supported Authorization: Bearer token
stopShip.impact: Any party that can reach the public API can enumerate app identities and correlate balances, deposits, spend, bonuses, and activity. The helper-only tests encode the disclosure instead of exercising the HTTP authorization boundary.
requiredBeforeCommit: Keep pricing and comparison public only if intentionally advertised; require management auth for stats and wallets
Make the dashboard use the existing embedded UI token/Bearer flow without putting credentials in URLs
Add full HTTP tests proving unauthenticated requests get 401 and authenticated requests get bounded data
Do not create fallback financial state on read

stopShip.title: Storage-cap provenance and headroom math can enlarge an explicit operator cap and still fill the disk
evidence: packages/core/config/loader.js:121 treats maxStorageBytes === the built-in 50 GiB value as proof that the cap was unset
packages/core/config/loader.js:119-128 derives 75%/90% from total blocks and ignores available/free blocks and existing non-HiveRelay use
An adversarial unit probe passed an explicit 50 GiB cap on a mocked 1 TiB disk with only 2 GiB available; resolveStorageCap changed it to 768 GiB
A 100 GiB mocked disk with 1 GiB available resolved an unset cap to 75 GiB
docker-compose.yml explicitly supplies --max-storage 50GB, so the equality/provenance collision is a real repository deployment path
A nonexistent custom storage path is measured at its nearest existing ancestor; the probe measured /, which can be the wrong future mount
packages/core/config/default.js:149-160 leaves eviction.enabled false, while the incident patch shortens minAgeMs; the default boot therefore does not proactively shed an already-over-cap store
stopShip.impact: An explicit resource designation can be silently expanded by hundreds of GiB, a nearly full volume can be treated as having ample headroom, and an already-pressured node can remain above the new cap. This contradicts the incident-fix safety claim.
requiredBeforeCommit: Carry explicit provenance from CLI, environment, and persisted config; numerical equality is not provenance
Preserve explicit 50 GiB semantics and persist an explicit value even when it equals the built-in default
For an unset cap, never increase the legacy 50 GiB default merely because the disk is large; use a safe min with available-space/reserve math
Create/verify the actual storage mount before statfs or fail closed when the intended device cannot be proven
Define and test recovery for usage already over cap; do not imply the 6-hour age change is active while eviction is disabled
Add tests for explicit-equals-default, low-available-space, pre-used volume, wrong ancestor/mount, restart provenance, and all production entry points

additionalFindings.title: Credits endpoints are disconnected from authoritative runtime state
additionalFindings.detail: Repository-wide inspection found no RelayNode construction or lifecycle assignment of creditManager or pricingEngine outside the new helper/tests. api-credits.js instead creates ephemeral default managers/engines on GET, so stock runtime can return authoritative-looking empty wallets and default prices rather than configured persistent state. Wire lifecycle-owned state or return an explicit disabled/unavailable response.
